findings.reason: with no declared edges a node can be dispatched against §2's translator before it exists, and §5's whole measure is defined "in COCOS 17 after translation".
findings.text: every section is emitted with an empty `data-links`, so although followup `f-ddc-001` says "§2 needs §1's quantity list, §3 needs §2, and §4 needs §3. §5 needs §2's translator ... and §1's census file", none of those edges exists in the plan's relationships; a dispatcher reading links sees five independent nodes and can start §3 or §5 before §2. Sibling plans in the same directory populate the attribute and the convention is available in this repo: `docs/plans/forward-solver-route-integrity.html` carries `data-links="forward-solver-route-integrity#s5"` on `s4` and `data-links="forward-solver-route-integrity#s4"` on `s5`, and `docs/plans/cocos-standalone-distribution.html` carries `data-links="imas-ambix:jt60sa-facility-mint#s2"`. This is the same exposure the earlier wiring-1 finding named for §5; it was answered by editing the followup prose, which leaves the relationship field empty and the mis-ordering reachable.

findings.reason: §5 decides another plan's reference equilibrium, and without a control that rejects a known-inconsistent source its confirm verdict cannot fail.
findings.text: §5's done-when has three clauses and no negative control: (1) the residual is zero on the analytic Solov'ev state and a 1 % FF′ perturbation is detected, (2) the measure is reported for DINA 105052/1, 105069/3, 105013/1 and CORSICA 130506/6, (3) "the reference choice of iter-passive-plasma-circuit §6 is confirmed or revised on that table". The 1 % FF′ clause is a sensitivity control on the instrument, not a control on the decision the section exists to make: nothing in §5 makes the measure see a source whose flux functions and flux map disagree at the edge, so a lenient or mis-normalised measure confirms the reference and iter-passive-plasma-circuit §6 check 3 is then rebuilt against it. Every other section declares its control in the plan's own idiom ("Literal negative control: ..."), which makes this omission measurable rather than stylistic.

findings.reason: §5's done-when (2) fixes the table's contents, and the author must either state which normalisation the IDS table uses or require both forms be reported before the numbers can be read against the parity chain's.
findings.text: §5 says it "reports it as an absolute current density and against the local profile current, so its numbers are comparable to the parity chain's", but the function it extends normalises differently: `nova/imas/mast_parity_chain.py::_profile_reproduction_residuals` documents "Each row is ``RMS(j_phi_nova - j_phi_grid) / max(abs(j_phi_grid))``" (line 408), a slice-global maximum, not the local profile current. A row normalised locally cannot be compared with a parity-chain row normalised by the slice maximum, so the stated purpose of the extension is not met by the stated form.

findings.reason: the derivation the sentence names exists in the same script, and no DD-read node consumes e_Bp from it, so no node is sent down a wrong path.
findings.text: §2 says `nova/scripts/identify_source_cocos.py::determine_digits` "already derives σ_Bp from ..., σ_ρθφ from ...; and e_Bp from the flux-loop 2π ratio", but `determine_digits` (line 801) returns only `sigma_bp` and `sigma_rho_theta_phi` plus diagnostics; the 2π ratio comes from `flux_loop_two_pi_ratio` (line 716) and is reduced to `e_bp` in the caller at line 1690. The capability exists in the cited script, so the mechanism is sound; the attribution is not exact. It is immaterial to the DD path, where §2 fixes e_Bp = 1 by DD version.

findings.reason: done-when (3)'s "search for either name under nova/, scripts/ and tests/ returning nothing" already forces that call site to change, so the omission cannot cause a silent pass.
findings.text: §2 lists the importers of `cocos_from_digits` as `tests/test_io_cocos.py` and `tests/test_mastcocos.py`, but the production caller is `nova/scripts/identify_source_cocos.py:1692` (`verdict = cocos_from_digits(...)`), which a rename of `determine_digits` into `nova_cocos` also has to move.
